items: the pilot may run on the RTX 3070 if it is free before the GTX 1660 (the user, 12 October); the stage-1 record names the card
the routing margin in chunks of 16 sequences in S75b's processes and the statistics pool StatsPool (host memory; the same value up to float64 summation order, CHECK B3)

--stats-workers by this driver's formula (workers_rule; the spec says only 'from the benchmark's host memory'): measured peaks (VmHWM) of the main process, one statistics worker and the data process, the evaluations held while the workers lag, and a budget from the machine's RAM (the user's figure), the co-running job's measured peak (--beside) and MemAvailable
records of one arm and seed from two cards (an ok record or a divergence on each) are not resolved: stage 1 / 2 refuse, the report marks the reading incomplete

order: stage 1 needs the driver's code, this card's benchmark and CUDA CHECK output committed; stage 2 needs the driver's code, the stage-1 record, every results file and this card's benchmark and CUDA CHECK output committed
CHECK B7 (lock-step at L = 1536): R = 1 as the runs, each seed alone, batch 8 on CUDA, REG3 in both register modes (the R = 2, batch-32 lock-step does not fit either card)

failed runs (rules added 2026-10-13, before the pilot, revised after four reviews): DIVERGED = the evaluation's logits not all finite (checked before anything else), the non-finite-loss check, or a NaN / inf in a statistic: an outcome, never retried or rerun, under any code, on any card; any other failure, including a process that ended without a record (an open start marker), is OPERATIONAL: rerun on the same seed, never a fresh seed, on whichever card runs the arm; an invocation stops at the first operational failure that survives the retry; operational failures in 2 invocations HALT the seed until the user clears it (--retry-halted, naming the invocations it clears) or the code changes before stage 2; a halt is never a STOP

the pilot: a value STOP as soon as a pilot run ends below 0.9 or diverges, whatever the other seed ('S = 4 is not usable at B'); a halted seed leaves the decision to the user; the record lists every invocation and each seed's card, and stage 2 reads the pilot from every card's committed results file

a code change: before stage 2, an unavoidable change needs a committed, dated note (--code-change-note, whenever another code has a stage-1 record or pilot entries) and the CUDA CHECKs, the benchmarks and the pilot (840-841) are rerun under it; stage 1 writes its record before its first run, so a later code supersedes the earlier one as soon as its stage 1 starts; a value STOP under any code is final (recomputed from every code's pilot records); stage 2 needs every complete stage-1 decision to PROCEED, SPLIT_THR from the pilot under its code; earlier records kept as s75b_stage1_record_<sha>.*, never pooled; a superseded code is never used again; once stage 2 has a record or failure, the code is frozen for good: a change halts the screen for the user, no outcome re-drawn; the code on disk is compared with the invocation's before and after every run: a change stops the invocation (nothing charged before a run; a run it overlapped is kept, marked code_changed, and the user decides: --code-changed-decision keep or rerun, recorded)

stage 2: a diverged ORACLE run counts as below 0.9 (UNTESTED); a diverged learned-arm run is not ROUTED (n stays 10); a diverged SINGLE run gives no GAP for its seed; a halted ORACLE or read-arm seed leaves validity or the reading incomplete until the user decides; the report gives no reading after a value STOP, a code change in stage 2, a superseded stage-2 code or an undecided run whose code changed

the benchmark: usability per arm (finished, the arm's cases passed, workers given); a stage runs the arms its card allows and names the rest; a benchmark may be rerun at any time (earlier files kept in bench_archive/; a crashed one counts as failed; each run record carries its benchmark); one card unusable or unavailable: the other runs everything (--machine fallback or fallback-3070, each with --reason in stage 2's meta and records); no card allows the pilot: S75b cannot start; no card allows an arm: the arm cannot run (ORACLE: validity incomplete; a read arm: the reading incomplete; SINGLE: no GAP; WIDE_SLOW: no paired rows); no configuration, R or batch change; the user decides

sync: with commits required, stages refuse unless git fetch succeeds, the checkout is neither behind nor ahead of its upstream, and every S75b JSON file in OUT is committed; results files are pushed whatever the decision, and as soon as stage 2 starts; --device cpu is for the CHECKs only

one invocation per card (locks per checkout and per machine for a stage's or a benchmark's whole run); both stages are pushed at their start; a stage refuses while another card's last invocation, as pushed, has not ended and runs any of its arms, unless the user states with --other-card-idle (recorded) that it was killed, after pushing that card's results file from its own machine; the pilot runs on one card; stage 2's --arms runs only the named arms of the machine (recorded)
every time written is UTC with its zone
